title: Employer Investment Fund (EIF) and Growth and Innovation Fund (GIF) Programme Level Evaluation: Final Report
file_title: Employer Investment Fund (EIF) and Growth and Innovation Fund (GIF) Programme Level Evaluation
description: This document describes an evaluation of the Employer Investment Fund (EIF) and Growth and Innovation Fund (GIF) programs, aimed at encouraging UK employers to invest in skills and innovation for economic growth. The evaluation, conducted by Ipsos MORI and the Institute for Employment Studies, used longitudinal surveys, qualitative interviews, and statistical impact analysis. Results indicated that while the programs maintained training volumes, they did not significantly boost employer training investment or immediate business performance. Some employer-led projects showed success, emphasizing the need for employer engagement in project design. The evaluation also explored the Propensity Score Matching approach for creating comparable samples in impact analysis, highlighting the importance of sample comparability. The UK Commission for Employment and Skills led the research, suggesting that longer-term evaluations and employer engagement are crucial for the sustainability and effectiveness of future skills investment activities.

title: Evaluation of UK Futures Programme Final Report on Productivity Challenge 3: Pay and Progression Pathways in Hospitality and Retail
file_title: Climbing the ladder: progression pathways in retail and hospitality
description: This document describes an evaluation of the UK Futures Programme's Productivity Challenge 3, which aimed to improve pay and progression in the hospitality and retail sectors. The evaluation, conducted by SQW and completed in August 2016, utilized qualitative methods such as interviews and observations. With a £1.2 million investment, the programme focused on reducing turnover and recruitment costs through better staff training and clear career progression paths. Although there were challenges like complex tool development and data sharing reluctance from employers, the evaluation highlighted the importance of certified learning, clear progression routes, and active engagement with both employers and employees. The document also explores strategies for enhancing pay and progression, including employer engagement, demonstrating investment returns, and using a variety of educational tools. It underscores the need for businesses to value their staff and for government support in spreading best practices. The UK Commission for Employment and Skills is noted as a leader in this area. The evaluation concludes that while most goals were met, the full impact is yet to be seen, and continued efforts are necessary, emphasizing the need for collaboration, communication, and investment in skills development.

title: Evaluation of the UK Futures Programme Final Report on Productivity Challenge 2: Management and Leadership in Supply Chains and Networked Organisations
file_title: Strengthening the links in the chain: Management and leadership in supply chains and networked organisations
description: This document describes an evaluation of the UK Futures Programme's Productivity Challenge 2, which aimed to enhance management and leadership within supply chains and networked organizations to improve productivity. The evaluation, led by Graham Thom and Katie MacLeod from SQW and managed by Hannah Hope from the UK Commission for Employment and Skills, used a methodological approach that included research questions, tables, and figures to measure progress. The results indicated advancements in leadership capabilities, increased demand for management skills, and growth in social capital. The evaluation concluded that engaging prime organizations and their supply chains was crucial, and that tailored, high-quality training was effective in raising management capabilities. However, challenges such as financial sustainability of projects and the need for evidence of return on investment were noted. The document also emphasized the importance of face-to-face interactions over online forums for increasing social capital and the role of intermediaries in facilitating engagement between primes and supply chain businesses.

title: Evaluation of the UK Futures Programme: Conclusions and Guidance
file_title: Evaluation of UK Futures Programme: conclusions and guidance
description: The UK Futures Programme (UKFP) was assessed for its role in addressing workforce productivity challenges through employer-led projects in sectors like construction and manufacturing. The evaluation, conducted by SQW, utilized desk reviews, stakeholder consultations, and Co-creation Labs to measure the program's success in promoting collaboration and innovation. Although the UKFP successfully engaged partners and linked to policy agendas, it faced issues with application timelines and inter-project collaboration. The program showed that modest public investment could leverage significant private sector engagement and behavior change. However, it encountered difficulties in broad employer engagement, iterative learning, and long-term sustainability due to its short-term nature and small scale. The evaluation recommended longer preparation phases, better application support, and strategies for sustained collaboration. Insights from the evaluation suggest the importance of high-profile leadership, flexibility, and demand-led solutions for future workforce development initiatives. The methodology and findings from the UKFP are proposed for adoption by Local Enterprise Partnerships to tackle local skills and productivity challenges.
